transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I'm having a really hard time at work. I do bookkeeping, and I just... I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. 

I end up staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves, even when I know I've already checked the numbers. I just get this overwhelming feeling that if I don't check it one more time, something bad is going to happen, and it'll be completely my fault. It's just gotten really exhausting.
When you’re going back over the spreadsheets, are you having specific thoughts that bother you or feel intrusive, like a fear that something terrible will happen if the numbers aren’t perfect?

Yeah, exactly. Even after I've checked and I know the numbers match, this thought just... keeps jumping in. I'll suddenly think that I missed one hidden mistake, like in payroll or the taxes, and that somebody's check won't go through because of me. Or that the firm will get in serious trouble. 

I really try to push the thought away and just move on, but it comes right back. It's like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore.
When these thoughts come up, do you feel driven to do something, like rechecking the numbers a certain way, counting, or repeating a phrase in your head to make the worry go away?

Yeah, like I mentioned, it's the rechecking. I just feel completely driven to go back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. I don't really repeat phrases or count, I just... I can't stop checking the work. 

That's why I end up staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I've already checked the numbers and they look fine, I just get this intense urge that I have to do it one more time. If I don't do it, I feel like something bad is definitely going to happen and it'll be my fault. Going back through the spreadsheet again is the only thing that makes that worry go away, at least for a little while.
Have these thoughts and the need to recheck things affected your life outside of work, like your relationships, sleep, or other activities?

Yeah, it really has. Um... it's actually causing major problems at work now, too. I recently missed a filing deadline because I was so stuck on rechecking the numbers, and I got called into a formal meeting about it. 

And outside of work... well, I've basically stopped going to my choir rehearsals. I also volunteer and have commitments at a youth center, but I've been missing those too. I just... I can't get out of the office on time to make it to any of them anymore. Everything else has just kind of stopped.
Have you noticed these kinds of thoughts or the need to do something to relieve the worry showing up in any other parts of your life, like at home or when you're around other people?

Um... no, not really. It's pretty much just the spreadsheets and the numbers at work. I don't really have those same kind of thoughts or the checking thing at home or anywhere else. It's just... it's just the work stuff that gets me stuck like that.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms are highly specific to their work environment and involve intrusive thoughts related to responsibility and perfectionism, followed by compulsive checking behaviors that significantly impair occupational and social functioning. This aligns more strongly with OCD (F42.9), especially given the absence of similar behaviors in other contexts, which makes generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) less likely.

inference_history.note: The patient presents with repetitive checking behavior, anxiety about potential negative consequences, and significant impairment in functioning. These symptoms are suggestive of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), though other anxiety-related disorders remain in the differential at this stage.

The patient's symptoms of persistent intrusive thoughts and repetitive checking behavior point towards Obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.9). However, generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) remains a candidate due to the worry about work performance and potential consequences. Adjustment disorder with anxiety (F43.22) is less likely given the repetitive compulsive behavior rather than a reaction to a specific stressor. Agoraphobia (F40.10) has not been supported by the current dialogue.
